text:
alex (frontend): Heads up — noticed a new regression on the console: hovering the legend in the heatmap tabs causes a 150–300ms main-thread freeze and spikes bundle parsing. Repro on prod and canary.

mira (eng-platform): ugh, saw alerts for LCP and increased TTFB from those pages. Any clue which commit pulled in a bigger chart lib? :thinking:

sam (infra): deployment graph shows a spike coinciding with 2026-03-19 bundle bump — looks like bundle grew by ~120KB gz.

alex (frontend): I bisected — the culprit is the legend component. It imports the full tiling util and an intl chunk synchronously. Code excerpt:

```js
// Legend.js (simplified)
import { computeTiles } from 'viz-tiler'; // 90KB pull
import 'chart-locales/en';
export default function Legend(...) { ... }
```

alex (frontend): computeTiles serializes a large array which triggers V8 parse spikes when hovered (it's constructing layout metadata on mouseenter).

jonathan (metrics): telemetry shows a strong correlation: sessions with legend interactions have 2.4x higher main-thread work. Trace ID example: trace:heatmap-2891.

mira (eng-platform): proposed mitigations: lazy-load Legend, memoize tile compute, and add a light-weight placeholder for hover. Also consider chunk-level split for i18n so chart locales don't pull for all routes.

sam (infra): agree. We should also look at our sourcemap pipeline — recent change to keep large source maps inline in CI artifact might be slowing the asset pipeline and making rollbacks painful. Noticed sourcemap upload times doubled.

alex (frontend): quick patch I tested locally:

```js
const Legend = React.lazy(() => import('./Legend'));
// in render
<Suspense fallback={<LegendStub/>}><Legend .../></Suspense>
```

alex (frontend): with that, hover freeze drops to ~30ms locally and bundle-parsing stays deferred until first hover.

mira (eng-platform): sounds good. Two rollout concerns: 1) users on slow networks might still hit first-hover cost; 2) we need to ensure telemetry captures first-load and subsequent loads separately.

jonathan (metrics): I'll add a probe: event heatmap.legend_lazy_load with timing and client_rtt tag. Also capture whether computeTiles was invoked and how long it took.

sam (infra): for canary, we should gate via a rollout flag so we can flip back quickly. Can we ship in a small canary to EU region only?

mira (eng-platform): yes — we have route-based flags. I'll create a canary rollout: heatmap-legend-lazy -> 10% EU. Canary ID heatmap-legend-2026-03-20.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started (id: heatmap-legend-2026-03-20) -> region: eu-west-1 -> targets: console-web-frontend (10%).

alex (frontend): FYI patch also moves computeTiles into a worker for big datasets:

```js
// spawn worker only when dataset > 2000 cells
if (data.length > 2000) {
  const w = new Worker(new URL('./tiler.worker.js', import.meta.url));
  w.postMessage(data);
}
```

mira (eng-platform): worker fallback is nice. For smaller datasets we still memoize. Also we should add a sampling rule in telemetry to avoid blowing up metrics if many clients hit first-load. jonathan?

jonathan (metrics): added sampling param to probe (sample_rate=0.2 by default, can raise in canary). Will send a quick dashboard update to track main-thread time by route and client RTT.

alex (frontend): another micro-optimization: switch to dynamic import for chart locales:

```js
if (needsLocale) import(`chart-locales/${locale}`).then(...)
```

alex (frontend): reduces initial parse by ~40KB for most users.

mira (eng-platform): action list: 1) alex to PR lazy Legend + worker + locale dynamic import, 2) jonathan to add telemetry probes & dashboard, 3) sam to monitor sourcemap pipeline and rollbacks, 4) me to create canary flag and coordinate EU rollout.

alex (frontend): PR opened -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/7890 (WIP). Tests failing on a snapshot; will fix.

sam (infra): re: sourcemaps — I'll revert inline map change for next deploy and add a retention TTL so uploads don't double. That should speed deploy and make hotfix rollout quicker.

mira (eng-platform): if PR looks good and canary metrics show main-thread improvement without new errors, we'll roll to 100% next week. Keep an eye on error rates — lazy-loading can hide init bugs.

alex (frontend): quick note: added local fallback to disable worker when WebWorker not supported (old safari).

jonathan (metrics): dashboard panel created: "Heatmap Legend — main thread & lazy-load latency". Sharing link in channel in 10m.

mira (eng-platform): perfect. If anyone sees odd console errors during canary, ping me directly and include the client tracing id. :thumbsup:

alex (frontend): thanks — will follow up after tests are green. :rocket:
